thread.title_full: Bronco defense aims to fix mistakes, but saw positives against Notre Dame - NewsBreak

author: JOHN WUSTROW
title: Bronco defense aims to fix mistakes, but saw positives against Notre Dame - NewsBreak
text:
By JOHN WUSTROW ,
16 hours ago
BOISE — It wasn’t perfect by any means, but the Boise State defense says it saw a lot it could build on in last weekend’s 28-7 loss to Notre Dame. For starters, the Broncos held the Fighting Irish offense to well under the 44.8 points per game they came in averaging.
And while missed tackles and blown pass coverages still reared their heads, the Broncos still saw some positives.
“I thought we played good,” said Boise State safety Ty Benefield, who led the Broncos with eight tackles. “Obviously there are things to fix but I really like how we are on that type of timing, just going after the ball and giving it our all and not caring who it was.”
Boise State (3-2, 1-0 Mountain West) will look to fix some of those mistakes, while building off what it was able to do well in South Bend as it returns to Mountain West play on Saturday with a home game against New Mexico (3-2, 0-1).
“There was no quit in our defense,” Boise State coach Spencer Danielson said. “Even missing a tackle, there were a couple third downs we didn’t execute or there was a lack of execution, we still found a way to get a stop. I’m proud of that, I’m proud of how our guys battled. Going into the game, I think they’re one of the most explosive offenses in the country. And what our guys did, there’s still multiple missed tackles that I know we’re better than.”
For the Broncos, the defensive play has been on a bit of an upswing as of late. Two weeks ago, the Broncos held Appalachian State, a team that entered the game with the No. 3 passing offense in the country, to just 65 passing yards, including two in the second half. Last week, the Irish came into the game having scored 56 points in back-to-back weeks against Power 4 opponents Purdue and Arkansas. The Broncos held them to half of that.
“I talked to some Notre Dame coaches after, and they were very complimentary about the effort and physicality we played with,” Boise State defensive coordinator Erik Chinander said. “Obviously when you’re playing in a game of that nature, where you’re playing a good team and a good program ... you got to limit your mistakes. You got to tackle well, they tackled better than we did. They created turnovers, we didn’t create turnovers. To me, on the defensive side of the ball, that’s what you have to do in a big game against another really good team.”
One bright spot for the Broncos defense came on the game’s first drive, which saw the Fighting Irish drive down to the Boise State goal line. Notre Dame went for it on a fourth and goal on the Boise State 1-yard line, but a group of Bronco tacklers took Notre Dame running back Jeremiyah Love down for a loss on the play, keeping the game scoreless early.
Trailing 7-0 in the second quarter, Boise State’s defense got another turnover on downs, when Notre Dame quarterback CJ Carr overthrew a receiver on fourth and 8 from the Bronco 28.
“They mean a lot because it’s very difficult to stop somebody on fourth and short,” Benefield said. “So, if you do that against a national ranked team and a good opponent, or even anybody, it says a lot.”
Of course, it wasn’t all positive for Boise State. It never is in a loss.
Love still had 103 rushing yards for the Irish, who put up 389 total yards of offense. Notre Dame had six offensive plays that went for more than 20 yards. On the longest play of the day, a 49-yard rush by Jadarian Price, the Notre Dame running back broke out of no less than five Boise State tackles on his way to the end zone.
That run extended the Irish lead to 28-7, effectively ending any dreams Boise State had for a comeback.
“The biggest thing I want to continue to focus on for our defense is that we got to find a way to get off the field on third and long,” Danielson said. “We have to get off the field on third and long. We lost a couple of third and longs that if we don’t, that game could swing differently because that’s like a turnover. There’s a couple plays there, especially in the second quarter and third quarter that we didn’t and that led to points.”
